title: The compressed spring stores energy
hook: Change compression and predict elastic potential energy.
misconception: elastic potential energy doubles when compression doubles, regardless of the stated relationship.
objective: Apply U = ½kx² to compare elastic potential energy when compression changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With an ideal spring with fixed stiffness, U = ½kx². When compression doubles, elastic potential energy becomes 4 times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model U = ½kx²; scaling exponent 2. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider an ideal spring with fixed stiffness, with a nonzero initial result. If compression triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on elastic potential energy?
recall.why: Apply U = ½kx² under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 9.
